channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Ciro Nogueira já apoiou Lula e Bolsonaro: veja trajetória do senador
item.description: Senator Ciro Nogueira, currently an ally of Bolsonaro and a leading opposition figure, has a political history of supporting various presidents since the 1990s, including Lula and Workers' Party governments, and has previously declared his vote for Lula. His trajectory reflects a long-standing presence in governmental coalitions, despite his current opposition to the Lula administration.

item.title: Cármen Lúcia critica violência de gênero em última sessão como presidente do TSE
item.description: Minister Cármen Lúcia concluded her presidency at the TSE by criticizing the 'barbaric' gender-based violence faced by women in positions of power during the Court's final session. She was honored by colleagues at the end of her term leading the electoral tribunal.

item.title: Trump disse que não considera invadir Cuba, diz Lula
item.description: Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva said that U.S. President Donald Trump told him, via an interpreter, that he has no intention of invading Cuba. The statement, made in Washington, aims to ease long-standing tensions between the two countries regarding Cuba.

item.title: Lula cita dosimetria e diz ter entregue a Trump lista de autoridades com vistos dos EUA suspensos
item.description: President Lula (PT) stated that he delivered to Donald Trump a list of Brazilian authorities whose U.S. visas are suspended, citing the approval of the dosimetry bill as a factor that could reduce sentences and facilitate entry permissions. He also joked with Trump about visas for Brazilian national team players during the 2026 World Cup, to be held in the U.S., Mexico, and Canada. Lula noted this is the second meeting between the two leaders to discuss bilateral issues.

item.title: STM diz que aumento de penduricalhos respeita decisão do STF
item.description: The STM states that the increase in penduricalhos for military judiciary magistrates complies with the STF's decision, following three resolutions passed in April that reclassified the Cumulative Jurisdiction Exercise Gratuity as indemnity, allowing payments above the constitutional ceiling. The change follows STF and CNJ/CNMP guidelines, per Joint Resolution No. 14/2026, and is supported by Law No. 13,096/2015.

item.title: Flávio diz que são ‘graves’ acusações contra Ciro Nogueira, aliado dos Bolsonaro
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) described the accusations against Ciro Nogueira (PP-PI), a longtime ally of Jair Bolsonaro, as 'grave' in relation to the Federal Police operation investigating irregularities at Banco Master. Nogueira, former minister and national president of the PP, is suspected of receiving R$300,000 in a 'monthly allowance' from banker Daniel Vorcaro and of presenting an amendment drafted by the bank’s staff to benefit the institution. Flávio emphasized the need for a rigorous and transparent investigation, expressing confidence in the rapporteurship of Minister André Mendonça at the Supreme Court.

item.title: Crusoé: Lula e Trump não falaram sobre Pix, CV e PCC?
item.description: President Lula stated that his meeting with Donald Trump did not cover the Pix system or the potential designation of PCC and Comando Vermelho as terrorist organizations. He said Trump 'did not touch on the subject' of Pix and noted he brought Finance Minister Dario Durigan specifically to address economic issues like this.

item.title: O afago de Lula em Messias antes de embarcar para encontro com Trump
item.description: President Lula offered support to Jorge Messias after his Senate rejection for the STF, framing the vote as a political rebuke from Congress rather than a judgment on his qualifications. Messias wishes to leave the AGU due to tensions with lawmakers and judges, but Lula urges him to stay, possibly reassigning him to lead the Ministry of Justice. The meeting took place before Lula's trip to Washington to meet with Trump.

item.title: Brasil e EUA ampliarão cooperação contra armas e lavagem de dinheiro
item.description: Finance Minister Dario Durigan announced that Brazil and the U.S. have advanced cooperation against organized crime, including remote container monitoring, seizure of over half a ton of illegal weapons, and more than one ton of synthetic drugs flowing from the U.S. to Brazil. The collaboration also includes financial intelligence sharing via Operation Hidden Carbon, linking Brazil’s Federal Revenue and the U.S. IRS to combat money laundering and tax evasion, with traced funds linked to Delaware.

item.title: Lula consegue 30 dias para negociar com Trump sobre tarifas
item.description: Lula left the White House meeting with Trump with a 30-day deadline to advance trade negotiations between Brazil and the U.S. Brazil presented data showing an average import tariff of 2.7% on U.S. goods, challenging U.S. overtariffs, and the trade deficit was highlighted as a central issue in the talks.

item.title: Lula e Trump não discutiram CV e PCC na Casa Branca
item.description: Lula confirmed that the Comando Vermelho and PCC were not discussed during his three-hour meeting with Trump at the White House, contrary to expectations of U.S. designation of Brazilian factions as terrorist groups. He proposed a multilateral working group to combat organized crime in Latin America, criticizing the traditional U.S. military-focused approach and advocating for economic alternatives for vulnerable populations. Lula also announced he will present a national plan against organized crime in Brazil next week.

item.title: Lula diz não acreditar em interferência de Trump nas eleições: ‘Quem vota é o povo brasileiro’
item.description: President Lula said he does not believe Donald Trump will interfere in Brazilian elections, emphasizing that 'the Brazilian people vote'. He stressed that national sovereignty must be respected and that Brazil-U.S. relations are sincere despite political differences.

item.title: 71,8% em SC defendem impeachment de ministros do STF, diz pesquisa
item.description: A Futura/Apex poll shows that 71.8% of voters in Santa Catarina support the impeachment of STF ministers, while 17.7% oppose it and 10.5% did not know how to respond. The survey, conducted with 800 voters from April 24 to 25, has a margin of error of 3.5 percentage points and a 95% confidence level.

item.title: 'Não precisamos inventar nada para a imprensa', diz Lula sobre ter pedido mudança em protocolo de encontro com Trump
item.description: President Lula explained that he requested a change in the protocol for his meeting with Trump to avoid a press conference before the talks, stating there's no need to 'invent anything for the press' and that the focus should be on substantive discussion. The meeting, lasting over three hours, ended without a press conference, following Lula's discomfort in a prior encounter in Malaysia.

item.title: Jorginho Mello é aprovado por 77,9% dos eleitores em SC, diz pesquisa
item.description: Santa Catarina Governor Jorginho Mello (PL) enjoys a 77.9% approval rating among state voters, according to a Futura/Apex poll conducted April 24–25 with 800 respondents. His administration is rated as 'excellent' or 'good' by 69.7%, while 18.5% disapprove and 3.5% did not respond. The survey has a 3.5 percentage point margin of error and 95% confidence level, and is registered with the TSE under BR-01971/2026.

item.title: Lula diz que Trump não terá ‘qualquer influência’ nas eleições brasileiras
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva stated that Donald Trump will have no influence on Brazil's 2026 elections, emphasizing that the vote belongs to the Brazilian people. He added that he expects Trump to act as U.S. president and respect Brazil's democratic choice.

item.title: Trump nem tocou no assunto do Pix, diz Lula após reunião na Casa Branca
item.description: Lula stated that Trump did not mention the Pix during a nearly three-hour meeting at the White House, despite expectations that the topic would be raised. The Brazilian president said he had included the Finance Minister in his delegation anticipating the discussion, but since Trump did not bring up Pix, Lula also avoided addressing it. The instant payment system is under commercial investigation by the U.S., which claims preferential treatment by Brazil's Central Bank disadvantages American payment service providers.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro diz considerar ‘grave’ ação da PF contra Ciro Nogueira, ex-ministro de seu pai
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) described as 'grave' the Federal Police operation targeting Senator Ciro Nogueira (PP-PI), former minister of Jair Bolsonaro, in an investigation linked to Banco Master and businessman Daniel Vorcaro. The PF executed search and seizure warrants in four states, including Nogueira’s Brasília residence, and froze R$ 18.8 million in assets, authorized by Supreme Court Minister André Mendonça. Flávio stressed the need for rigorous and transparent investigation, expressing confidence in the rapporteurship of the minister appointed by his father.

item.title: EUA e Brasil vão criar grupo de trabalho para discutir tarifas nos próximos 30 dias, anuncia Lula
item.description: President Lula announced that Brazil and the U.S. will establish a working group to discuss the removal of U.S. tariffs on Brazilian products within the next 30 days. The announcement was made during a press conference at the Brazilian Embassy in Washington, following a meeting with Donald Trump. Lula also emphasized the approval of the critical minerals bill and Brazil’s openness to international partnerships for rare earth exploration.

item.title: Lula diz esperar que Trump um dia faça um sistema como o PIX e que americano não tocou no tema durante reunião
item.description: Lula stated that Donald Trump did not bring up the topic of PIX during their meeting at the White House, despite having brought the Finance Minister to discuss it. He jokingly said he hopes Trump will one day create a similar instant payment system, noting that many American companies already use such technology. PIX has been under commercial investigation in the U.S., viewed as a threat to credit card giants and dollar dominance in global trade.

item.title: Trump dá à União Europeia prazo até 4 de julho para implementar acordo comercial com EUA
item.description: U.S. President Donald Trump has given the European Union a July 4 deadline to implement the trade agreement reached last July, warning that tariffs would rise significantly if the bloc fails to fulfill its commitment to reduce tariffs to zero. Trump described the deal as 'the greatest trade deal of all time' and linked the deadline to the 250th anniversary of American independence. Although the EU Parliament has delayed ratification pending details on U.S. trade policy, negotiators say they are making progress, with a next meeting scheduled for May 19.

item.title: “Se ele tentou interferir nas eleições, ele perdeu. Porque eu ganhei”, diz Lula
item.description: President Lula (PT) stated he does not fear external interference in Brazil's 2026 elections, saying that if Donald Trump attempted to interfere in the 2022 elections, he lost because Lula won. Lula noted that during the 2022 Brazilian election, the U.S. president was Joe Biden, not Trump.

item.title: Lula celebra discussão positiva de ‘tabus’ com Trump e anuncia grupos de trabalho: ‘Satisfeito’
item.description: Lula praised a nearly three-hour conversation with Donald Trump on 'taboo' topics such as organized crime, announcing working groups for cooperation in economy, mineral exploration, and security. He advocated for economic alternatives to narcotrafficking, criticizing the U.S. militarized approach and proposing a South American and global coalition. The meeting took place in Washington after a White House press event was canceled, and both sides described it as productive and friendly.

item.title: Lula diz que facções não foi tema em conversa com Trump e que o combate ao crime organizado não deve envolver 'base militar'
item.description: Lula stated that his conversation with Trump did not include discussions about labeling Brazilian criminal factions as terrorist groups, and emphasized that combating organized crime requires economic alternatives, not military bases. He argued that as long as poverty and demand exist, drug trafficking will persist, and proposed an international task force led by Brazil to address the issue through shared responsibility.

item.title: 'Trump não vai mudar o jeito dele de ser por causa de uma reunião comigo', diz Lula ao comentar guerras
item.description: Lula said his meeting with Trump at the White House was an important step in strengthening Brazil-U.S. relations, despite clear differences in international policy views, particularly regarding Iran, Venezuela, and UN Security Council reform. He stressed that he does not expect Trump to change his behavior due to the meeting, but advocated dialogue as a more effective and humane alternative to war. Lula also commented on the prolonged Ukraine war and reiterated his opposition to armed conflicts, emphasizing that talking is cheaper and less destructive.

item.title: PL da Dosimetria: Moraes já negou redução de penas para dezesseis condenados
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes rejected sixteen requests for sentence reduction from those convicted of the January 8 attacks, ruling that the Dosimetry Bill, though approved by Congress, has not yet been promulgated and is not in force. The requests were deemed 'prejudiced' under the Court’s Internal Rules, not ruling on the merits, leaving the door open for future re-filing if the law is eventually published.

item.title: Lula diz que tratou com Trump assuntos que pareciam 'tabus'
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva said he discussed topics considered 'taboo' with Donald Trump during a three-hour meeting at the Brazilian Embassy in Washington. Lula noted that Trump praised him as 'very dynamic' in a social media post, while he shared photos of the encounter on his Instagram profile.

item.title: “É melhor ele rindo do que de cara feia”, diz Lula sobre Trump
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) said he suggested Donald Trump smile more in photos during their White House meeting, noting that Trump looks better laughing than with a stern face. The comment was made during a press briefing with ministers on Thursday, the 7th. Lula emphasized the importance of image in diplomacy and implied that a smiling demeanor could improve public perception of the encounter.

item.title: Após reunião com Trump, Lula diz que terras raras são questão de 'soberania nacional'
item.description: Following a meeting with Donald Trump at the White House, President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva stated that the approval of the critical minerals bill by the Chamber of Deputies treats the issue as a matter of national sovereignty. He emphasized that Brazil aims not only to export these resources but to be the primary beneficiary of their wealth, inviting American, Chinese, German, Japanese, and French companies to partner in mining, processing, and production. The nearly three-hour meeting is seen as a key step toward normalizing bilateral trade relations after U.S. tariffs and sanctions.

item.title: ‘Discutimos assuntos que pareciam tabus’, diz Lula sobre encontro com Trump
item.description: Lula said his meeting with Trump was very satisfactory because they discussed topics considered taboo, including organized crime and the flow of U.S. weapons to Brazil. He emphasized that Trump stated he does not plan to invade Cuba and reaffirmed respect for Brazilian democracy and sovereignty, refusing to discuss internal elections with foreign leaders. Lula also noted they talked about the need for UN Security Council reform, where the U.S. holds veto power and other countries are merely supporting actors.

item.title: Lula diz ter aconselhado presidente dos EUA a sorrir: 'Trump rindo é melhor do que de cara feia'
item.description: Lula said he advised Donald Trump to smile during their White House meeting, stating that 'Trump smiling is better than with a stern face'. He added that Trump found the comment amusing and they discussed the 2026 World Cup, with Lula joking about not revoking visas for Brazilian players. Lula emphasized that, except for Brazilian sovereignty, all topics are open for discussion with the U.S.

item.title: Reunião de Lula e Trump nos EUA termina após cerca de 3 horas
item.description: The meeting between Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and U.S. President Donald Trump took place at the White House on Thursday, April 7, lasting approximately three hours. The session concluded without a press briefing in the Oval Office, with no joint public statements issued following the discussion.

item.title: Trump diz que reunião com Lula foi "muito boa" e promete novos encontros bilaterais
item.description: Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva met with U.S. President Donald Trump at the White House in Washington, D.C., in a meeting lasting about three hours, followed by lunch. They discussed trade, security, and economic cooperation, with Trump describing the meeting as 'very good' and promising future bilateral engagements.

item.title: “Bordando a Democracia”: livro reúne vozes femininas em prol da participação política das mulheres
item.description: The book 'Embroidering Democracy', launched by the Superior Electoral Court on April 7, gathers reflections from women on democracy, human rights, and female political participation, inspired by forums led by Minister Cármen Lúcia in 2024 and 2025. The work likens democratic construction to embroidery — a continuous, collective, and careful process — and includes voices from ministers, parliamentarians, artists, journalists, and Indigenous leaders, such as Benedita da Silva, Luiza Trajano, and Marisa Monte. Organized into three sections, it addresses affirmative actions, gender-based political violence, and women’s underrepresentation in Brazilian politics.

item.title: Lula concede entrevista após reunião com Trump
item.description: Lula met with Trump at the White House in a meeting that lasted nearly three hours, including a lunch, after which no joint press statement was issued due to the meeting running over time. The meeting aimed to normalize trade relations between Brazil and the U.S. following U.S. tariffs on Brazilian products and sanctions against Brazilian officials.

item.title: Flávio publica vídeo de IA de Lula e Trump sobre terras-raras
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) shared an AI-generated video on X depicting President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva kneeling in the Oval Office offering 'rare earths' to Donald Trump, in a satirical take on their upcoming May 7 meeting in Washington. The video references U.S. pressure on Brazil to designate criminal factions like PCC and Comando Vermelho as terrorist organizations, and aligns with Flávio’s prior advocacy for closer Brazil-U.S. ties under Trump. The post’s caption read: 'The Trump-Lula meeting leaked online! Is it real?'

item.title: Conversa de Lula com Trump foi muito positiva e esclarecedora, avaliam ministros
item.description: Lula's ministers described the meeting between the Brazilian president and Donald Trump as very positive, productive, and enlightening, noting the president's optimism after the lunch at the White House. The nearly three-hour discussion opened prospects for future agreements, with aides characterizing the tone as frank and constructive. Lula is expected to give an interview shortly at the Brazilian embassy in Washington.

item.title: Elogio de Trump, tour na Casa Branca, três horas de reunião: como foi o encontro de Lula com o presidente americano
item.description: Lula was received by Donald Trump at the White House during his first official visit under the Trump administration. The meeting lasted about three hours and covered topics such as trade and tariffs, with Trump praising Lula as 'dynamic' and calling the meeting 'very good' and 'productive'. The joint press conference was canceled, and Lula will speak with journalists at the Brazilian Embassy.

item.title: Motta: Debate sobre redução de jornada “não foi criado por ser ano eleitoral”
item.description: House Speaker Hugo Motta stated that the debate over reducing the maximum workweek in Brazil was not created due to the 2026 elections, calling it an longstanding issue. Speaking in Paraíba, he dismissed claims that the topic is being politicized for electoral gain.

item.title: Planalto pede que ministros não se posicionem sobre operação que mira Ciro Nogueira
item.description: The Planalto Palace instructed ministers not to comment on the Federal Police operation targeting Senator Ciro Nogueira, to avoid perceptions of retaliation by the Lula government after the Senate rejected Jorge Messias’ STF nomination. The PF alleges that banker Daniel Vorcaro commissioned a constitutional amendment benefiting Banco Master, which Nogueira introduced but was not approved. Nogueira’s defense denies wrongdoing and challenges the legitimacy of investigations based on third-party messages.

item.title: TSE conclui que não houve fraude à cota de gênero em Salvaterra (PA)
item.description: The Superior Electoral Court (TSE) upheld the decision of the Pará Regional Electoral Court (TRE-PA) rejecting allegations of gender quota fraud by the Liberal Party (PL) in Salvaterra (PA) during the 2024 elections. Candidate Thaina Vieira da Serra conducted effective campaign activities, received donations in campaign materials, and obtained five valid votes, which the court deemed consistent with local realities, dismissing the claim of a fictitious candidacy.

item.title: Ao falar de Flávio, Haddad diz que ‘investigações sobre escândalos vão esclarecer que campanhas o Master financiou’
item.description: Fernando Haddad stated that investigations into the Banco Master scandal should clarify which campaigns the bank financed and reveal Flávio Bolsonaro’s connections to the case, aiming to bring transparency and counter misinformation about the senator. He emphasized that the Federal Revenue, Federal Police, and Public Prosecutor’s Office must act to investigate involved lawmakers, noting the case will have electoral impact. Haddad also denied a significant increase in the tax burden under Lula’s government.

item.title: Lula orientou toda a comitiva brasileira a falar apenas português em reunião com Trump
item.description: Lula directed his entire entourage, including English speakers, to speak only Portuguese during the meeting with Trump at the White House, according to a TV Globo source. The meeting, originally scheduled for 12:15 p.m. Brasília time, was delayed by over an hour at Lula’s request, who preferred a closed-door session before speaking to the press. Topics discussed include trade, PIX, organized crime, critical minerals, geopolitics, and Brazilian elections, amid ongoing tensions from the Middle East war and recent diplomatic incidents.

item.title: Flávio vence Lula em 2º turno em SP, diz Futura/Apex
item.description: A Futura/Apex poll shows Flávio Bolsonaro would defeat Lula in a hypothetical São Paulo runoff with 46.7% to 39.4%, based on 1,200 voters surveyed April 27-29. Lula ties technically with Ronaldo Caiado or Romeu Zema in alternative runoffs, within the 2.8-point margin of error. In the first round, Flávio and Lula are statistically tied, with Flávio slightly ahead in both tested scenarios.

item.title: Por que Lula não quis falar com a imprensa antes do encontro com Trump?
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva requested the White House alter its press protocol so that journalists could only attend after his meeting with Donald Trump, breaking from the usual practice of pre-meeting access to the Oval Office. The move aimed to avoid unexpected or uncomfortable questions before the encounter, particularly given the history of tensions between Lula and Trump on issues such as climate, democracy, and trade. Lula had just met with Malaysia’s prime minister, where he also maintained a tightly controlled media schedule.

item.title: Na despedida, ministra Cármen Lúcia reafirma luta pela democracia e igualdade feminina
item.description: Minister Cármen Lúcia concluded her final day as president of the TSE in a session marked by tributes, reaffirming her commitment to democracy and women's participation in positions of power. She emphasized the importance of the fight for gender equality and left office with a legacy of firm, diligent, and serene leadership. The new TSE leadership will be headed by Minister Nunes Marques, with André Mendonça as vice-president, starting next Tuesday (12).

item.title: Quem são os membros da comitiva de Lula e Trump no encontro que acontece na Casa Branca
item.description: Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva met with U.S. President Donald Trump at the White House in a meeting that began with a private conversation in the Oval Office, at Lula’s request, before press presence. The Brazilian delegation includes five ministers: Mauro Vieira (Foreign Affairs), Dario Durigan (Finance), Márcio Rosa (Development, Industry and Foreign Trade), Alexandre Silveira (Mines and Energy), and Wellington César Lima e Silva (Justice and Public Security), plus Federal Police Director-General Andrei Rodrigues. On the U.S. side, attendees include J.D. Vance, Susie Wiles, Scott Bessent, Jamieson Greer, and Howard Lutnick, with discussions focused on trade, rare earths, organized crime, and big tech regulation.

item.title: Lula pede para imprensa só entrar no Salão Oval depois de reunião com Trump
item.description: President Lula requested that the White House allow press to enter the Oval Office only after his meeting with Trump, reversing the traditional protocol to avoid pre-meeting questions as happened in their prior encounter in Malaysia. The request was accepted by Trump, and the meeting has already lasted over an hour with officials from both sides present. Following the meeting, both leaders will make statements to the press, followed by a lunch hosted by Trump.

item.title: Escândalo do Master: Ação da PF contra Ciro torna tóxica aliança com PP-União Brasil para a eleição
item.description: The Federal Police operation against Ciro Nogueira, president of the PP, linked to the Banco Master scandal, threatens the viability of the PP-Union Brazil alliance for the 2026 elections, given that Union Brazil politicians were also previously implicated. Despite the federation’s strength — 101 federal deputies — formalizing the alliance now risks bringing corruption allegations onto the campaign trail, especially with Ciro seen as a potential running mate for Flávio Bolsonaro. The PT is unlikely to gain directly from the episode due to its reliance on PP alliances in state races and its historical inability to effectively weaponize corruption narratives against opponents.

item.title: A pedido de Lula, imprensa só entrará no Salão Oval após encontro com Trump
item.description: Lula requested that journalists only enter the Oval Office after his meeting with Trump, reversing standard protocol. The move was driven by fears that Trump might embarrass Lula on camera, as he had done with Zelensky and Ramaphosa. Brazil’s team sought to avoid a media 'ambush' during the White House visit.
